1.question:
A company uses AWS CloudFormation to manage an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The instances are in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. The company wants to treat its infrastructure as immutable.
A DevOps engineer must implement a solution to replace two EC2 instances at a time whenever operating system configuration updates are needed or when new Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) are needed. A minimum of four EC2 instances must be running whenever an update is in progress.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
1.A: Modify the CloudFormation template to include a StackPolicy. Designate an AutoScalingReplacingUpdate policy to control the update. Specify MinInstancesInService of 4 and MaxBatchSize of 2. Whenever a software update is needed, alter either or both of the ImageId and UserData of the AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate and update the stack.
1.B: Modify the CloudFormation template to include an UpdatePolicy attribute for the Auto Scaling group. Include the AutoScalingRollingUpdate policy with MinInstancesInService of 4 and MaxBatchSize of 2. Whenever a software update is needed, alter either or both of the ImageId and UserData of the AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate and update the stack.
1.C: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to 4. Create an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group that has an in-place deployment type. Select Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group for the environment configuration. Whenever a new revision is available, create a new CodeDeploy deployment that has a deployment configuration of CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime.
1.D: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to 4. Create an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group that has a blue/green deployment type. Select Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group for the environment configuration. Whenever a new revision is available, create a new CodeDeploy deployment that has a deployment configuration of CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime.

2.question:
A company has converted all of its Amazon EC2 instances to use Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) rather than IMDSv1. The company needs to implement a solution to enforce IMDSv2 for any EC2 instances that are launched or modified in the future to use IMDSv2.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
2.A: Create an EC2\_INSTANCE\_LAUNCHING lifecycle hook. Notify an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Program the Lambda function to call the EC2 ModifyInstanceMetadataOptions API operation to set the HttpTokens parameter to required.
2.B: Turn on AWS Config. Create an AWS Config rule that detects whether EC2 instances are using IMDSv2. Set up an automatic remediation action to run an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to configure EC2 instances that are using IMDSv1 to use IMDSv2.
2.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to monitor the EC2 RunInstances operation. Configure the EventBridge rule with AWS API Call via CloudTrail as the event type and EC2 as the AWS service. Specify as the target an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that configures EC2 instances to use IMDSv2.
2.D: Create an IAM policy to deny the EC2 RunInstances action if the MetadataOptions.HttpTokens=required condition is not met. Attach this policy to all IAM roles that EC2 instances will use.

3.question:
A company has configured AWS CodeDeploy to automatically update an AWS Lambda application. The deployment has failed a few times recently. A DevOps engineer needs to implement a solution to immediately notify the company's application team by email when failures occur in the future.
The DevOps engineer creates an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for failed deployments.
What should the DevOps engineer do next to meet the notification requirement in the MOST operationally efficient manner?
3.A: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send a message to the SNS topic when a deployment state changes to the failed deployment state. Subscribe the application team's email address to the SNS topic.
3.B: In CodeDeploy, create a trigger for failed deployments. Specify the SNS topic as the destination. Subscribe the application team's email address to the SNS topic.
3.C: In CodeDeploy, create a trigger for failed deployments. Specify the SNS topic as the destination. Create a Lambda function that sends an email message when an event is published to the SNS topic.
3.D: Turn on AWS CloudTrail logging in the company's AWS account. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Subscribe the queue to the SNS topic. Use the queue to send the email notification.

4.question:
A company uses AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to access its AWS accounts. The company manages the AWS accounts with AWS Organizations. In the central network account, the company recently created a transit gateway to handle routing between all AWS accounts. The company wants to use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the transit gateway with the company's current and future AWS accounts.
What should a DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?
4.A: Within the organization's management account, activate AWS RAM for trusted access and create a resource share with a resource type of Transit Gateway. Select the existing transit gateway as the resource. Specify the central network account as the principal.
4.B: Within the central network account, activate organizational sharing in AWS RAM. Within the organization's management account, create a resource share with a resource type of Transit Gateway. Select the existing transit gateway as the resource. Specify the central network account as the principal.
4.C: Within the organization's management account, activate AWS RAM for trusted access. Within the central network account, create a resource share with a resource type of Transit Gateway. Select the existing transit gateway as the resource. Specify the organization ID as the principal.
4.D: Within the central network account, activate organizational sharing in AWS RAM and create a resource share with a resource type of Transit Gateway. Select the existing transit gateway as the resource. Specify the organization ID as the principal.

5.question:
A large company has acquired a small company. The large company has an organization in AWS Organizations. The large company needs to integrate the small company's single AWS account into the organization with minimal impact to the applications that are deployed in the small company's account.
The large company has deployed AWS Control Tower in its organization and wants to enroll the small company's account in AWS Control Tower. The large company's AWS Control Tower configuration includes a security OU, a sandbox OU, and a new destination OU that is set up for the small company's migration. Each company is using AWS Config as part of its account management strategy.
Which combination of steps should a DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements?
5.A: Create a landing zone in the security OU of the large company's AWS Control Tower landing zone. Provide the account's email address, the account owner's first and last name, and the name of the landing zone created in the security OU to complete the AWS Control Tower Account Factory enrollment request.
5.B: Create an AWS Config conformance pack that contains the policies that are currently applied to the large company's account. Use AWS Config to assess the impact that enrollment in AWS Control Tower will have on the small company's account. Delete the configuration recorder and delivery channels from the AWS Config settings of the small company's account.
5.C: Create and apply SCPs in the destination OU to restrict the types of resources that can be created in the small company's account. Assess the impact of the applied SCPs on the small company's account. Delete existing SCPs in the small company's account.
5.D: Create an AWSControlTowerExecution role in the small company's account. Provide the account's email address, the account owner's first and last name, and the destination OU to complete the AWS Control Tower Account Factory enrollment request.
5.E: Enroll the OU of the small company's account in the large company's AWS Control Tower environment. Specify the destination OU in the large company's AWS Control Tower landing zone as the receiving OU in the request.

6.question:
A company uses AWS Organizations to manage 400 AWS accounts. A DevOps engineer is deploying a new feature to all member accounts in all AWS Regions by using AWS CloudFormation StackSets. The deployment is taking a long time.
Which combination of actions will lead to the LOWEST deployment time for future deployments?
6.A: Set the maximum concurrent accounts percentage to 25.
6.B: Set the maximum concurrent accounts number to 25.
6.C: Set the Region concurrency to Parallel.
6.D: Set the Retain Stacks option to True.
6.E: Set the Region concurrency to Sequential.

7.question:
A company has deployed an application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk by using an all-at-once deployment method. The deployment failed recently because of an application misconfiguration and resulted in significant downtime.
To prevent such downtime in the future, a DevOps engineer needs to revise the deployment method while maintaining the application performance. The DevOps engineer must ensure that application versions are consistently configured across all instances while minimizing downtime.
Which deployment solution will meet these requirements?
7.A: Switch to a rolling deployment with additional batch strategy for future application updates.
7.B: Switch to an immutable deployment strategy for future application updates.
7.C: Switch to a blue/green deployment strategy for future application updates.
7.D: Switch to a rolling deployment strategy for future application updates.

8.question:
A company's legacy application uses IAM user credentials to access resources in the company's AWS Organizations organization. A DevOps engineer must ensure that new IAM users cannot be created unless the employee who creates the IAM user is on an exception list.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
8.A: Attach an Organizations SCP with an explicit deny for all iam:CreateUser actions with a condition that includes StringNotLike for aws:username with a value of the exception list.
8.B: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule with a pattern that matches the iam:CreateUser action with an AWS Lambda function target. The function will check the user name and account against an exception list. If the user is not on the exception list, the function will delete the user.
8.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule with a pattern that matches the iam:CreateAccessKey action with an AWS Lambda function target. The function will check the user name and account against an exception list. If the user is not on the exception list, the function will delete the user.
8.D: Attach an Organizations SCP with an explicit deny for all iam:CreateAccessKey actions with a condition that excludes StringEquals for aws:username with a value of the exception list.

9.question:
A company needs to scan code changes for security issues before deployment and must prevent noncompliant code from being deployed. The company uses an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that starts when code changes occur. The code changes occur many times each day.
The company's security team supports a third-party application for code scans and has provided command-line integration steps to submit code scans. The code scan step requires a user name and password.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?
9.A: Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. Configure the user name and password in an environment variable. Use the user name and password to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.
9.B: Upload the user name and password in an encrypted JSON file to an Amazon S3 bucket that has a specific policy to allow only administrators to read the file. Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. Use the user name and password from the file in Amazon S3 to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.
9.C: Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. Store the user name and password as a string in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Read the string from Parameter Store. Use the user name and password to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.
9.D: Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. Store the user name and password as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Read the secret from Secrets Manager. Use the user name and password to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.

10.question:
An ecommerce company is looking for ways to deploy an application on AWS that satisfies the following requirements:
Has a simple and automated application deployment process.
Has minimal deployment costs while ensuring that at least half of the instances are available to receive end-user requests.
If the application fails, an automated healing mechanism will replace the affected instances.
Which deployment strategy will meet these requirements?
10.A: Use AWS Systems Manager to configure the application layer to use rolling deployments as a deployment strategy. Add an Application Load Balancer. Enable automatic healing on the application layer.
10.B: Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment and configure it to use Auto Scaling and an Application Load Balancer. Use rolling deployments with a batch size of 50%.
10.C: Use AWS CodeDeploy with Auto Scaling and an Application Load Balancer. Use a blue/green deployment strategy. Enable an Application Load Balancing health check to report the status of the application, and set the Auto Scaling health check to ELB.
10.D: Use AWS CodeDeploy with Auto Scaling and an Application Load Balancer. Use the CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime deployment strategy. Enable an Application Load Balancing health check to report the status of the application, and set the Auto Scaling health check to ELB.

11.question:
A company manages its AWS accounts by using AWS Organizations. A Development OU is configured for the company's development team to use. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution to provide access to the Development OU for the development team.
The development team needs programmatic access and access to the AWS Management Console for development activities. The development team must not have access to manage IAM permissions. The company has an existing self-managed Active Directory identity provider connection established with AD Connector. Access and security policies must be enforced by an AD group that includes the development team members.
What should the DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?
11.A: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets in the management account for deployment to the Development OU. Configure a stack to create a development team IAM group and users, place the users in the group, assign the AWS managed PowerUserAccess IAM policy to the group, and provide programmatic access and access to the AWS Management Console. Programmatically create new AD Connectors in each target account. Synchronize the development team AD group with the development team IAM group.
11.B: Ensure that all features are enabled in Organizations. Enable AWS IAM Identity Center in the management account. Select the existing self-managed AD directory with AD Connector as the identity store. Create a permission set that uses the AWS managed PowerUserAccess IAM policy. Assign the permission set to the self-managed development team AD group in IAM Identity Center. Connect the development team AD group to the Development OU accounts.
11.C: Ensure that all features are enabled in Organizations. Enable AWS IAM Identity Center in the delegated administrator account. Select the existing self-managed AD directory with AD Connector as the identity store. Create a permission set that uses the AWS managed AdministratorAccess IAM policy. Assign the permission set to the self-managed development team AD group in IAM Identity Center. Connect the development team AD group to the Development OU accounts.
11.D: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets in the management account for deployment to the Development OU. Configure a stack to create a development team IAM group, assign users to the group, and create a custom IAM policy that allows all development activity except management of IAM permissions. Create a script that provides programmatic access and access to the AWS Management Console. Synchronize the AD Connector between the self-managed development team AD group and the development team IAM group. Run the script in each Development OU account.

12.question:
A company hosts an application in North America. The application uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. A team of analysts in Europe generates real-time reports by using the DB cluster. The analysts must have access to the most up-to-date data. A DevOps engineer discovers that the generation of reports is much slower for users in Europe than for users in North America.
What should the DevOps engineer do to resolve this issue?
12.A: Create an Aurora global database. Use the existing DB cluster as the primary cluster, and add a secondary cluster in an AWS Region in Europe. Configure the users' machines to point to the Aurora reader endpoint in Europe.
12.B: Use Amazon DynamoDB global tables in an AWS Region in Europe. Set up continuous replication between the DB cluster and the DynamoDB table by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Configure the users' machines to point to the DynamoDB table in Europe.
12.C: Create cross-Region Aurora Replicas in North America, and activate synchronous replication. Configure the users' machines to point to the Aurora reader endpoint in North America.
12.D: Create an Amazon DynamoDB table in Europe. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to configure replication between the DB cluster and the DynamoDB table. Configure the users' machines to point to the DynamoDB table in Europe.

13.question:
A company needs to migrate a legacy internal web application from its on-premises data center to its AWS account. The company already has configured a VPC that has two public subnets and two private subnets. The VPC has outbound internet connectivity.
The application can run on only a single server at a time. Other existing on-premises applications need to communicate with the migrated application. The company needs the migrated application to automatically recover.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements?
13.A: Configure an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule that allows traffic from the company's on-premises data center. Associate the web ACL with the Application Load Balancer.
13.B: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that is associated with the private subnets in the VPC. Create a launch template to install the legacy application on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group that uses the launch template. Attach the ALB to the Auto Scaling group.
13.C: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that is associated with the public subnets in the VPC. Create a launch template to install the legacy application on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group that uses the launch template. Attach the ALB to the Auto Scaling group.
13.D: Configure an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule that denies traffic from the company's on-premises data center. Associate the web ACL with the Application Load Balancer.
13.E: Update the Auto Scaling group capacity limits to have a minimum capacity of 1, a maximum capacity of 1, and a desired capacity of 1.
13.F: Update the Auto Scaling group capacity limits to have a minimum capacity of 2, a maximum capacity of 3, and a desired capacity of 2.

14.question:
A company has an Amazon S3 bucket that stores log data. The log data is a combination of AWS logs and custom logs from a variety of AWS sources and external sources. Most of the log data is in a JSON format, and some of the log data is in a CSV format. The S3 bucket receives new objects each night. Several of the external logs are sourced directly from customer systems.
A DevOps engineer needs to be able to directly analyze data from all the JSON logs each morning.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?
14.A: Create a second S3 bucket. Modify the sources of the log data to route CSV logs to the initial S3 bucket and to route JSON logs to the second S3 bucket. Configure the second S3 bucket as a data source for Amazon Athena. Schedule an AWS Glue crawler to run daily on the second S3 bucket. Run Athena queries directly on the second S3 bucket to conduct the required analysis.
14.B: Create a second S3 bucket. Schedule a daily S3 Batch Operations job to move the JSON objects to the second S3 bucket. Configure the second S3 bucket as a data source for Amazon Athena. Schedule an AWS Glue crawler to run daily on the second S3 bucket. Run Athena queries directly on the second S3 bucket to conduct the required analysis.
14.C: Configure the S3 bucket as a data source for Amazon Athena. Create an AWS Glue crawler with an include pattern of \*.json. Schedule the AWS Glue crawler to run daily after the S3 bucket receives the new objects. Run Athena queries directly on the S3 bucket to conduct the required analysis.
14.D: Configure the S3 bucket as a data source for Amazon Athena. Create an AWS Glue crawler with an exclude pattern of \*.csv. Schedule the AWS Glue crawler to run daily after the S3 bucket receives the new objects. Run Athena queries directly on the S3 bucket to conduct the required analysis.

15.question:
A company uses federated access for its AWS environment. The company creates and manages IAM roles by using AWS CloudFormation from a CI/CD pipeline. All changes should be made to the IAM roles through the pipeline.
The company's security team discovers that out-of-band changes are being made to the IAM roles. The security team needs a way to detect when these out-of-band changes occur.
What should a DevOps engineer do to meet this requirement?
15.A: Use Amazon Inspector rules to detect and notify when an AWS CloudFormation stack has a configuration change.
15.B: Use AWS CloudTrail to detect and notify when an AWS CloudFormation stack detects a configuration change.
15.C: Use an AWS Config rule to detect and notify when AWS CloudFormation drift detection identifies a configuration change.
15.D: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to detect and notify when an AWS CloudFormation stack has a configuration change.

16.question:
A company protects its web application by using an AWS WAF web ACL that is associated with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Internal clients and external clients access the web application. The company needs to apply a rate limit on requests to the application. The limit must be higher for requests from internal clients than for requests from external clients.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements?
16.A: Create an AWS WAF rate-based rule for the internal clients. Set the rate limit to an appropriate value. Configure a scope-down statement to apply to requests that have the INTERNAL label. Create another AWS WAF rate-based rule. Set the rate limit to an appropriate value for requests that do not have the INTERNAL label.
16.B: Create an AWS WAF IP set that contains the IP addresses of the internal clients. Create an AWS WAF rule to match requests from the IP set and to apply a label of INTERNAL.
16.C: Create an AWS WAF IP set that contains the IP addresses of the internal clients. Create an AWS WAF rate-based rule. Define a separate rate limit for internal clients and external clients. Configure a scope-down statement to apply the internal limit to requests that have the INTERNAL label.
16.D: Create an AWS WAF rule group. Configure rules to match the IP addresses of the internal clients and to apply a label of INTERNAL.
16.E: Create two AWS WAF rule groups. In the rule group for internal clients, include a scope-down statement to match requests that have the INTERNAL label. In the rule group for external clients, do not include a scope-down statement. Create an AWS WAF rate-based rule in the internal rule group. Set the rate limit to an appropriate value. Create an AWS WAF rate-based rule in the external rule group. Set the rate limit to an appropriate value for requests that do not have the INTERNAL label.

17.question:
A company has an application and a CI/CD pipeline. The CI/CD pipeline consists of an AWS CodePipeline pipeline and an AWS CodeBuild project. The CodeBuild project runs tests against the application as part of the build process and outputs a test report. The company must keep the test reports for 90 days.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
17.A: Add a new stage in the CodePipeline pipeline. Configure a test action type with the appropriate path and format for the reports. Configure the report expiration time to be 90 days in the CodeBuild project buildspec file.
17.B: Add a report group in the CodeBuild project buildspec file with the appropriate path and format for the reports. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the reports. Configure the report group as an artifact in the CodeBuild project buildspec file. Configure the S3 bucket as the artifact destination. Set the object expiration to 90 days.
17.C: Add a report group in the CodeBuild project buildspec file with the appropriate path and format for the reports. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the reports. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function to copy the reports to the S3 bucket when a build is completed. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to expire the objects after 90 days.
17.D: Add a new stage in the CodePipeline pipeline after the stage that contains the CodeBuild project. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the reports. Configure an S3 deploy action type in the new CodePipeline stage with the appropriate path and format for the reports.

18.question:
A company is launching an application that stores raw data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Three applications need to access the data to generate reports. The data must be redacted differently for each application before the applications can access the data.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
18.A: Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an AWS Lambda function that is invoked by object creation events in the raw data's S3 bucket. Program the Lambda function to redact data for each application. Publish the data on the Kinesis data stream. Configure each application to consume data from the Kinesis data stream.
18.B: Create an S3 bucket for each application. Configure S3 Same-Region Replication (SRR) from the raw data's S3 bucket to each application's S3 bucket. Configure each application to consume data from its own S3 bucket.
18.C: Create an S3 access point that uses the raw data's S3 bucket as the destination. For each application, create an S3 Object Lambda access point that uses the S3 access point. Configure the AWS Lambda function for each S3 Object Lambda access point to redact data when objects are retrieved. Configure each application to consume data from its own S3 Object Lambda access point.
18.D: For each application, create an S3 access point that uses the raw data's S3 bucket as the destination. Create an AWS Lambda function that is invoked by object creation events in the raw data's S3 bucket. Program the Lambda function to redact data for each application. Store the data in each application's S3 access point. Configure each application to consume data from its own S3 access point.

19.question:
A company uses AWS Organizations to manage its AWS accounts. The company wants its monitoring system to receive an alert when a root user logs in. The company also needs a dashboard to display any log activity that the root user generates.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements?
19.A: Enable AWS Config with a multi-account aggregator. Configure log forwarding to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
19.B: Create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs metric filter to match root user login events. Configure a CloudWatch alarm and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send alerts to the company's monitoring system.
19.C: Create an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard that uses a CloudWatch Logs Insights query.
19.D: Create an AWS CloudTrail organization trail. Configure the organization trail to send events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
19.E: Create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to match root user login events. Configure the filter to forward events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure the SNS topic to send alerts to the company's monitoring system.
19.F: Create an Amazon QuickSight dashboard that uses an Amazon CloudWatch Logs query.

20.question:
A company is running two applications: application-a and application-b. The applications run on separate Amazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux. The instances for application-a and application-b are in the same VPC and are spread across multiple Availability Zones. The application-a instances run in different Availability Zones than the application-b instances. Each instance is associated with an IAM role that is based on the application that the instance hosts.
A development team needs to allow application-a to have read/write access to all data in a storage solution. The development team must allow application-b to have read/write access to only the /data/application-b directory.
The development team deploys an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system with mount targets in each Availability Zone. The EFS file system is already mounted on the application-a instances. A DevOps engineer must complete the configuration.
Which combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements?
20.A: On each EC2 instance, create a user for the application that the instance is running. Ensure that each user has a unique user ID and group ID. Mount the file system by using the user account. Change the ownership of the mount directory path to correspond to the application.
20.B: For application-b, configure the file system policy to allow the instance role used for application-b to mount and write to the file system. Include a condition statement to ensure that the application role can access the file system through only the access point.
20.C: For each application, create an additional EFS mount target in each Availability Zone. Configure the mount target policy to allow the role for the application to mount and write to the file system. Include a condition statement to ensure that the application role can access the file system through only the access point.
20.D: In AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM), create a resource share for the EFS file system. Share the file system with IAM roles for application-a and application-b.
20.E: Create an EFS access point for application-b with the root directory path of /data/application-b. Set the root directory creation permissions to 0755.

21.question:
A company has a VPC that consists of a public subnet and a private subnet. The company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in the private subnet. An Application Load Balancer is in the public subnet and distributes traffic to the EC2 instances.
The company has enabled Amazon GuardDuty for the account. The company's DevOps team has a list of external IP ranges that is updated each day. The list is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the account. A DevOps engineer needs to configure GuardDuty to create a GuardDuty finding when traffic to the application originates from an IP range in the external IP range list.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
21.A: Configure a threat list in GuardDuty. Set the source as the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to refresh the threat list in GuardDuty to match the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket.
21.B: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to retrieve the most recent list of external IP ranges from the S3 bucket. For each IP range in the list, configure the Lambda function to create a GuardDuty finding filter on the publicIp filter attribute.
21.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to retrieve the most recent list of external IP ranges from the S3 bucket. For each IP range in the list, configure the Lambda function to create a GuardDuty finding filter on the localIp filter attribute.
21.D: Configure a trusted IP list in GuardDuty. Set the source as the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to refresh the trusted IP list in GuardDuty to match the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket.

22.question:
A company uses AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild to build and deploy its applications. The company needs to add an automated step for unit testing in the software deployment pipeline. The package management tool that the company uses for its programming language runs the tests for the applications.
Which combination of actions should a DevOps engineer take to add the new step to the pipeline?
22.A: Use CodeBuild to run the automated tests.
22.B: Integrate the CodeBuild step into the CodePipeline pipeline.
22.C: Use Amazon CodeGuru to run the automated tests.
22.E: Integrate the Amazon CodeGuru step into the CodePipeline pipeline.

23.question:
A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets in two Availability Zones. A DevOps engineer must reconfigure the architecture to increase the reliability of the application. The application must have internet access for periodic updates, but the EC2 instances must not be directly accessibly from the internet.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
23.A: Launch new EC2 instances to run in an Auto Scaling group in newly created private subnets in the two Availability Zones. Create a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the Auto Scaling group as the target for the ALB. Create NAT gateways in the public subnets. Update the route tables for the private subnets to route all outbound traffic to the NAT gateways.
23.B: Launch new EC2 instances in newly created private subnets in the two Availability Zones. Create a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). Create a target group for the ALB. Include the EC2 instances in the target group. Create NAT gateways in the public subnets. Update the route tables for the public subnets to route all outbound traffic to the NAT gateways.
23.C: Launch new EC2 instances to run in an Auto Scaling group in newly created private subnets in the two Availability Zones. Create a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). 65.question:
A company uses AWS Organizations. The company needs to provide a set of packaged libraries for member accounts to use. The company's tooling team has an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that consists of the source Git repository and an AWS CodeBuild project that packages the libraries. The tooling team needs to update its CodePipeline pipeline to provide the packaged libraries to the member accounts.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
65.A: Use AWS CodeArtifact to create a single domain. For each package, create a repository in the newly created domain. Configure repository policies for the member accounts. Configure the CodeBuild project to publish the packaged libraries to CodeArtifact in the post-build phase.
65.B: Use AWS CodeArtifact to create a domain and a repository for each package. Configure domain policies for the member accounts. Configure the CodeBuild project to publish the packaged libraries to CodeArtifact in the post-build phase.
65.C: Use AWS CodeArtifact to create a single domain. For each package, create a repository in the newly created domain. Configure a domain policy for the member accounts. Configure the CodeBuild project to publish the packaged libraries to CodeArtifact in the post-build phase.
65.D: Use AWS CodeArtifact to create a domain and a repository for each package. Configure repository policies for the member accounts. Configure the CodeBuild project to publish the packaged libraries to CodeArtifact in the post-build phase.

66.question:
A company uses AWS Organizations to manage its AWS accounts. The company's DevOps team analyzes the CPU and memory metrics of the company's Amazon EC2 instances and applies an Underutilized tag to some resources in the member accounts. The DevOps team needs to prevent users in the member accounts from modifying or deleting these tags.
What is the MOST operationally efficient way to meet this requirement?
66.A: In the member accounts, deploy an AWS Lambda function by using AWS CloudFormation StackSets. Configure the Lambda function to run the DescribeTags API operation and to update the tag values if there is a mismatch. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the Lambda function every 30 minutes.
66.B: In the member accounts, deploy an AWS Lambda function by using AWS CloudFormation StackSets. Configure the Lambda function to run the DescribeTags API operation and to update the tag values if there is a mismatch. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the Lambda function every time a CreateTags or DeleteTags API event occurs.
66.C: Create a tag policy that denies the CreateTags API action and the DeleteTags API action for the Underutilized tag to authorized principals. Attach the tag policy to the OU in the management account.
66.D: Create an SCP that denies the CreateTags API action and the DeleteTags API action for the Underutilized tag to non-authorized principals. Attach the SCP to the OU in the management account.

67.question:
A company has an application that monitors user activity on the company's website and mobile apps. The application uses Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS) as a write-through cache and uses an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database for longer storage. When the application receives a request to record a user's action, the application writes to the Redis cluster and the database at the same time. Internal recommendation applications consume the data to produce content recommendations for each user.
During peak periods, the recommendation applications cannot generate recommendations for users because of stale and missing data. The Redis cache is configured with cluster mode turned off, and the database is configured with a single read replica.
The company wants to ensure that the recommendation applications can generate content recommendations during peak periods. A DevOps engineer already has created a new ElastiCache (Redis OSS) cluster with cluster mode enabled.
What should the DevOps engineer do next to meet the company's requirements?
67.A: Create a scheduled auto scaling policy for the Redis cluster's ElastiCachePrimaryEngineCPUUtilization metric. Configure the auto scaling policy to add read replicas to the Redis cluster. Update the recommendation applications to use the database's read replica endpoint instead of Redis.
67.B: Create a target tracking auto scaling policy for the Redis cluster's ElastiCachePrimaryEngineCPUUtilization metric. Configure the auto scaling policy to increase and decrease shards to the Redis cluster. Update the recommendation applications to use the cluster's configuration endpoint to access Redis.
67.C: Create a target tracking auto scaling policy for the Redis cluster's ElastiCachePrimaryEngineCPUUtilization metric. Configure the auto scaling policy to increase and decrease shards to the Redis cluster. Update the recommendation applications to use the cluster's read replica endpoint to access Redis.
67.D: Create a scheduled auto scaling policy for the Redis cluster's ElastiCachePrimaryEngineCPUUtilization metric. Configure the auto scaling policy to add read replicas to the Redis cluster. Update the recommendation applications to use the cluster's configuration endpoint to access Redis.

68.question:
A company runs an application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) and stores container images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). The company uses AWS CodeDeploy to automatically deploy the application and apply updates.
A DevOps engineer needs to implement a solution that automatically rolls back a deployment if the deployment process fails. The solution also must provide the DevOps engineer with an immediate notification if a deployment fails.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST number of changes to the infrastructure?
68.A: Configure CodeDeploy to roll back when the process fails. Configure Amazon EventBridge to send the DevOps engineer an email message when deployment fails.
68.B: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that has a detail type of CodeDeploy Instance State-change Notification. Configure the rule to send a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure the SNS topic as an alarm. Configure rollback to occur when alarm thresholds are met.
68.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that has a detail type of CodeDeploy Deployment State-change Notification. Configure the rule to send a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure CodeDeploy to roll back when the process fails. Subscribe the DevOps engineer to the SNS topic.
68.D: Configure Amazon CloudWatch metrics for CodeDeploy to create a CloudWatch alarm. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to send a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure CodeDeploy to roll back when the process fails. Subscribe the DevOps engineer to the SNS topic.

69.question:
A company has a mobile application that makes HTTP API calls to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB routes requests to an AWS Lambda function. Many different versions of the application are in use at any given time, including versions that are in testing by a subset of users. The version of the application is defined in the user-agent header that is sent with all requests to the API.
After a series of recent changes to the API, the company has observed issues with the application. The company needs to gather a metric for each API operation by response code for each version of the application that is in use. A DevOps engineer has modified the Lambda function to extract the API operation name, version information from the user-agent header, and response code.
Which additional set of actions should the DevOps engineer take to gather the required metrics?
69.A: Configure AWS X-Ray integration on the Lambda function. Modify the Lambda function to create an X-Ray subsegment with the API operation name, response code, and version number. Configure X-Ray insights to extract an aggregated metric for each API operation name and to publish the metric to Amazon CloudWatch. Specify response code and application version as dimensions for the metric.
69.B: Modify the Lambda function to write the API operation name, response code, and version number as a log line to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Configure a CloudWatch Logs metric filter that increments a metric for each API operation name. Specify response code and application version as dimensions for the metric.
69.C: Modify the Lambda function to write the API operation name, response code, and version number as a log line to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Configure a CloudWatch Logs Insights query to populate CloudWatch metrics from the log lines. Specify response code and application version as dimensions for the metric.
69.D: Configure the ALB access logs to write to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Modify the Lambda function to respond to the ALB with the API operation name, response code, and version number as response metadata. Configure a CloudWatch Logs metric filter that increments a metric for each API operation name. Specify response code and application version as dimensions for the metric.

70.question:
A company has a web application that users access over the internet. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The ALB is associated with a security group that allows traffic from the internet. The web application has a local cache on each EC2 instance.
During a recent security incident, requests overloaded the web application and caused an outage for the company's customers. In response to the incident, the company added Amazon CloudFront in front of the web application. All customers now access the web application through CloudFront.
A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that routes all requests through CloudFront. The solution also must give the company the ability to block requests based on the content of the requests, such as header or body information.
Which combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements?
70.A: Create an AWS WAF web ACL. Associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distribution. Create rules for each type of traffic that the company wants to block.
70.B: Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service for the ALB. Configure the endpoint service to allow requests from CloudFront. Update the web application origin in CloudFront to use the newly created endpoint service's DNS name.
70.C: Create a CloudFront origin access control (OAC) for the web application. Update the web application origin in CloudFront to use the OAC. Update the ALB rules to check for the OAC and return an HTTP 403 error if the OAC header is not present.
70.D: Create new ALB listener rules on the existing listeners. Configure the new rules to allow or reject incoming traffic based on whether a custom header matches a value defined by the DevOps engineer.
70.E: Create an AWS Firewall Manager security policy. Attach the security policy to the CloudFront distribution. Use the security policy to attach AWS WAF rule groups for each type of traffic that the company wants to block.

71.question:
A DevOps engineer is deploying an AWS Service Catalog portfolio using AWS CodePipeline. The pipeline should create products and templates based on a manifest file in either JSON or YAML, and should enforce security requirements on all AWS Service Catalog products managed through the pipeline.
Which solution will meet the requirements in an automated fashion?
71.A: Use the AWS Service Catalog deploy action in AWS CodeDeploy to push new versions of products into the AWS Service Catalog with verification steps in the CodeDeploy AppSpec.
71.B: Use an AWS Lambda action in CodePipeline to run a Lambda function to verify and push new versions of products into the AWS Service Catalog.
71.C: Use the AWS Service Catalog deploy action in AWS CodeBuild to verify and push new versions of products into the AWS Service Catalog.
71.D: Use an AWS Lambda action in AWS CodeBuild to run a Lambda function to verify and push new versions of products into the AWS Service Catalog.

72.question:
A company runs its software products as microservices on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) clusters that are powered by Amazon EC2 instances. The instances are launched from publicly available Amazon ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2 AMIs that AWS maintains and updates.
During a compliance review, a DevOps team receives an urgent request to install a custom security package on the Amazon ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2 AMIs before the AMIs are launched in Amazon ECS. The team must implement a solution that does not affect the ECS task launch time. The solution must validate the security package before a new image can be used. The team also needs access to image build logs that capture specific error messages in real time.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
72.A: Use EC2 Image Builder to configure a new image pipeline. Create a new image recipe that uses AWS managed Amazon ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2 as the base image. Configure custom security package installation. Configure an EC2 Image Builder component to validate and test the built images. Access EC2 Image Builder logs through Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use CloudWatch filters to capture specific error messages.
72.B: Use AWS Systems Manager. Ensure that Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is pre-installed on the cluster EC2 instances. Create a Systems Manager Automation custom runbook that can run a script to install the custom security package and run test cases. Create a new EC2 tag key and value. Ensure that all new EC2 instances launch with the tag. Configure Systems Manager Automation to run the custom runbook on all instances that have the EC2 tag. For logging, pre-install the Amazon CloudWatch agent to stream the user data operations in real time. Use CloudWatch filters to capture specific error messages.
72.C: Use EC2 Image Builder to configure a new image pipeline. Import the current Amazon ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2 AMI as the base image. Create a new image recipe that uses the imported base image. Configure custom security package installation. Configure an EC2 Image Builder component to validate and test the built images. Access EC2 Image Builder logs through Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use CloudWatch filters to capture specific error messages.
72.D: Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the custom security package. Use EC2 user data to add a script to pull the package from Amazon S3 and install the package. Add validation scripts in the user data to run test cases. For logging, pre-install the Amazon CloudWatch agent to stream the user data operations in real time. Use CloudWatch filters to capture specific error messages.

73.question:
A company has resources in an AWS account. The resources are deployed to multiple AWS Regions. In the AWS account, the company also has IAM users that access the AWS Management Console. The company has configured an AWS CloudTrail multi-Region trail to log management events for read and write activity to an Amazon S3 bucket.
A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that tracks all AWS Management Console login failures. When a console login failure occurs, the company's security team must receive an email notification in near real time.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
73.A: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team's email address to the SNS topic. In the us-east-1 Region, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses AWS events as the event source. Use a filter for console login failure events. Configure the SNS topic as the rule's target.
73.B: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses AWS events as the event source. Create an AWS Lambda function. Write Lambda function code to match console login failure events from inbound data from EventBridge. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team's email address to the SNS topic. Configure the Lambda function to publish to the SNS topic.
73.C: Create an AWS Lambda function to process CloudTrail logs from the S3 bucket. Use S3 event notifications to invoke the Lambda function when a new object is created in the S3 bucket. Write Lambda function code to parse the logs from Amazon S3 and match console login failure events. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team's email address to the SNS topic. Configure the Lambda function to publish to the SNS topic.
73.D: Create an Amazon Athena table from the CloudTrail logs in the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the AWS SDK to query the Athena table. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke the Lambda function every 60 minutes. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team's email address to the SNS topic. Configure the Lambda function to publish to the SNS topic when a failed login is detected in the CloudTrail logs.

74.question:
A company stores purchase history in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company needs other workloads that run on AWS to react to data changes in the table.
The company has enabled a DynamoDB stream on the table. Three existing AWS Lambda functions have an event source mapping configured for the DynamoDB stream. The company's application developers plan to add other applications that will need to react to changes in the table. A DevOps engineer must design an architecture that will give the additional consumers this functionality.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?
74.A: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create a new Lambda function that uses the existing DynamoDB stream as an event source. Configure the new Lambda function to post those events to the SQS queue. Update the original Lambda functions to react to entries in the SQS queue. As other applications need the events, configure the applications to use the SQS queue as an event source.
74.B: Configure the DynamoDB table to use on-demand capacity mode. Increase the memory of the Lambda functions. Configure the Lambda functions to use provisioned concurrency.
74.C: Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create a new Lambda function that uses the existing DynamoDB stream as an event source. Configure the new Lambda function to post those events to the Kinesis data stream. Update the original Lambda functions to subscribe to records in the Kinesis data stream. As other applications need the events, configure the applications to use the Kinesis data stream as an event source.
74.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge event bus. Create a new Lambda function that uses the existing DynamoDB stream as an event source. Configure the new Lambda function to post those events to the event bus. Update the original Lambda functions to react to events in the event bus. As other applications need the events, configure the applications to use the event bus as an event source.

75.question:
An ecommerce company is running an application on AWS. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The database layer is hosted on an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Amazon Route 53 DNS records point to the ALB.
The company needs to create a standby disaster recovery solution in an additional AWS Region. The company cannot make any changes to the application code.
Which combination of actions will meet these requirements with the LOWEST cost?
75.A: Configure a failover routing policy for the application DNS entry.
75.B: Create a cross-Region read replica of the DB instance in the new standby Region.
75.C: Provision the ALB and the Auto Scaling group in the new standby Region. Set the desired capacity to match the desired capacity in the active Region.
75.D: Migrate the database layer to Amazon DynamoDB. Configure global replication to the new standby Region.
75.E: Configure a geolocation routing policy for the application DNS entry.
75.F: Provision the ALB and the Auto Scaling group in the new standby Region. Set the desired capacity to 1.
